newsitem.title: INDIA: At least seven killed in Kashmir blast - agencies.
newsitem.headline: At least seven killed in Kashmir blast - agencies.

text.p: Seven relatives of a campaign worker for Kashmir's ruling National Conference party were killed in a powerful blast on Monday, news agencies said.
They quoted officials as saying suspected Moslem militants triggered the blast at the residence of Ghulam Hassan Nadeef in the southern Kashmir district of Anantnag.
The United News of India (UNI) said Nadeef was not in the house at the time of the blast. Senior police officials have rushed to the site of the blast, it reported.

The attack came two days after Kashmir's newly-elected Chief Minister Farooq Abdullah told separatist militants to surrender their arms within 30 days. There has been no official response from the rebels.
Abdullah's National Conference gained an absolute majority after last month's assembly elections in India's state of Jammu and Kashmir, the first polls there in nine years.
Kashmir has been the cause of two of the three wars between predominantly Hindu India and Pakistan since the two nations gained independence from Britain in 1947.
Police and hospital sources say at least 20,000 people have been killed in six years of separatist violence. Abdullah says the toll was closer to 50,000.
Dozens of separatist groups have been fighting for complete independence or merger with neighbouring Pakistan since the revolt broke out in 1990.
